title: Implement CFA3-native shared CUDA compatibility fabric
goal: Provide one CFA3-owned structured CUDA compatibility fabric to every current and future CFA3 application, with AMD HIP and Intel SYCL/OpenCL target lowerings, build/runtime compatibility inspection, explicit portability classifications, and no Spectral Compute SCALE build/runtime dependency.
requirements: CUDA is a backend interface, not a capability.
One central shared CFA3-native functional core serves every current and future CFA3 application; application-local compatibility cores are forbidden.
Spectral Compute SCALE is not a build, runtime, binary-loading, installer or activation dependency.
CUDA source is analyzed through the bounded structured CFA3 CUDA IR frontend before target lowering.
AMD supported-subset translation targets admitted ROCm/HIP and is classified FULL_EQUIVALENCE only for that admitted subset.
Intel supported-subset translation targets SYCL/Level Zero primarily and OpenCL secondarily and is classified FUNCTIONALLY_REDUCED with explicit limitations.
Every target result is FULL_EQUIVALENCE, FUNCTIONALLY_REDUCED or UNAVAILABLE.
Unknown CUDA semantics, runtime symbols and nvcc options fail closed; no silent option or backend fallback.
Build plans and runtime maps are inspection/preparation artifacts and never authorize execution.
PTX, CUBIN, FATBIN, closed CUDA binary compatibility, full CUDA/nvcc/Driver/CUDA-X parity are not claimed.
Translation execution requires explicit workload policy; HRB remains placement/lease authority and Hardware Safety retains precedence.
Native NVIDIA CUDA remains independent and primary where admitted.
Physical Current Host or target-host evidence is required before runtime promotion.
Capability baseline remains 175 with no new architectural authority.
